question: In most women, the uterus lies in an anteverted and anteflexed position within the lesser pelvis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The commonest uterine position is anteverted–anteflexed. Retroversion (uterus tilts backward) occurs in ~20% of women and is usually a normal variant unless fixed by adhesions (e.g., endometriosis).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! The normal uterine position is anteverted (the uterus tilts forward relative to the vaginal axis) and anteflexed (the fundus bends forward on the cervix). Retroversion and retroflexion are common normal variants but occur in a minority.
